chunks: Safwan from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār said:
I asked Abā Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) about the Muṭamattiʿ when he shaves his head, what is permissible for him? So he (peace be upon him) said: Everything except for the women.

key_terms.النِّسَاءَ: The women (specifically wives in this context)
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعِ: The Muṭamattiʿ, one who performs Tamattuʿ Hajj

ai.seo_question: What is permissible for a Muṭamattiʿ after shaving his head during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for the Muṭamattiʿ, shaving the head (ḥalq) rather than trimming (taqsīr) fully lifts the minor Ihram restrictions, permitting all marital relations except sexual intercourse. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that ḥalq is the complete marker of exiting the state of Ihram for Tamattuʿ, distinguishing it from the partial exit associated with trimming.
